finding.claim: /admin/drop ignores the Authorize result, so any authenticated user (any role) can reach a DROP TABLE built by concatenating the raw `t` form value, which is also SQL injection.
finding.source: HTTP request form value `t` (r.FormValue, query string or POST body), read at api.go:27. Attacker is any authenticated user, since the role check result is discarded at api.go:26.

trace.note: /admin/drop is registered on DefaultServeMux with no auth middleware in this file
caller user loaded from request context via userFrom
Authorize(u, "dba") return value discarded; a non-dba user falls through
raw FormValue "t" concatenated into DROP TABLE and passed to runSQL; no allowlist, no parameterization; stacked statements such as `x; DROP ...` also pass through

finding.guards_checked: Authorize at api.go:13-20 is correct in isolation but its error is ignored at api.go:26 (no return/throw). userFrom at api.go:22 panics on a nil context value, so as shipped with no middleware the handler panics before reaching the SQL; this is a crash, not a bypass. Exploitability depends on an upstream auth middleware (not in this repo) that populates the context "user" for any authenticated caller. No allowlist on the table name, no parameterized query, no CSRF protection (method not restricted, FormValue accepts query string, so a GET link can trigger it under cookie auth).

verdict.guard_found: Authorize at api.go:13-20 exists but its error is discarded as a bare statement at api.go:26, so it does not block anything. No allowlist, parameterization, or path containment on the value at api.go:27. The only other guard is userFrom at api.go:22, which panics on a nil context user, so the handler crashes before the SQL runs in this repo. No auth middleware is registered for /admin/drop at api.go:44.
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate: the Authorize result is discarded at api.go:26 and the raw form value is concatenated into DROP TABLE at api.go:27, with no effective guard. Reachability is not established from this repo, because /admin/drop is registered with no middleware at api.go:44 and the handler panics at api.go:22 unless an unseen upstream middleware populates the "user" context value for authenticated callers, so the "any authenticated user" attacker depends on code outside the repo.

finding.claim: The /admin/drop and /admin/vacuum routes are registered directly on http.DefaultServeMux with no authentication or authorization wrapper, so route-level protection depends entirely on a middleware that is not present in this codebase.
finding.source: Any unauthenticated network client reaching :8083 (api.go:46 binds all interfaces).
finding.sink: http.HandleFunc registrations at api.go:44-45 exposing dropTable and vacuum

trace.note: ListenAndServe on :8083 without TLS or a wrapping handler

finding.guards_checked: No middleware wrapping in main; the only guards are in-handler (userFrom and Authorize). userFrom panics without context user, which blocks unauthenticated access as shipped but is not an intentional control. Reported as PLAUSIBLE because the real guard may live in a server or proxy layer outside this repo.

verdict.guard_found: userFrom (api.go:22) panics when no *User is in the request context and is called at api.go:25 and api.go:32, so anonymous requests abort before runSQL; Authorize (api.go:13-20) is checked in vacuum (api.go:33-36) and its result is discarded in dropTable (api.go:26), so dropTable has no effective role check for any caller whose context carries a user.
verdict.reason: The trace matches the code (api.go:44-46 register both routes with no wrapper), and as shipped an anonymous request panics in userFrom (api.go:22, 25) before runSQL (api.go:27, 37), but whether a user is ever placed in the context depends on middleware outside this repo, so reachability cannot be decided here. The stronger in-repo defect the candidate omits is that dropTable discards Authorize's error (api.go:26) and concatenates r.FormValue("t") into SQL (api.go:27), which would let any authenticated non-DBA user drop tables if such a context is set.
